body: I had the chance to visit the beautiful Kanneliya Rain Forest about two weeks ago with a few of my colleagues during our study tour to Galle. This was actually my third visit to this amazing forest reserve, and it still felt just as refreshing and peaceful as the first time.The walk through the lush greenery, the sound of flowing streams, and the cool forest air make it a perfect nature escape. Our local guide, Mallika, was brilliant, her life story and deep knowledge about the forest, its flora, fauna, and conservation efforts made the experience even more meaningful. That was truly a highlight of the visit.We ended the day with a simple yet delicious village-style lunch, the perfect way to wrap up a great day surrounded by nature. Highly recommended for anyone who loves nature and tranquillity!
title: A Refreshing Escape into Nature at Kanneliya Rain Forest 🌿

body: I did the longest trek on offer, the 12 km to and from Kabbale peak. It was hot and humid like I have never experienced. I have never leaked/sweat so much while in a resting state. I was smart enough to wear trousers but dumb enough to choose tear aways... There are leeches like you wouldn't believe, and they are absolutely unlike the ones I thought existed from watching 1990s summer camp movies. They could scale a building, so unless you want to be bitten, long thick socks are a must as are trousers, and I would tuck your shirt in. Bring deet spray to spray your boots and help keep them off. The peak climb is tough; there really is no trail and we effectively were bushwacking our way through. You would need a relatively high level of fitness for this and no injuries or frailties. Even though I arrived at 7 AM, I saw, and heard, little bird life, which another reviewer noted too. I think this might have been better on the easier, lower altitude trails: more birds around and also the tree branches aren't so high. I did not see any mammals at all, though I could see tree movement on one two occassions indicating monkeys. Note that the walks apart from Kabbale peak are mostly if not wholly maintained footpaths (though I think Warerfall 2 might have the last 1 km or so through forest trails). On these maintained footpaths, leeches are not a concern.The entry price to the park was 1240. The guide price was 3200 to Kabbale for foreigners. My guide was very nice, and her english was good enough to point out animals and such along the way. What animals she did point out I absolutely never would have noticed myself (mostly small lizard types and a cool snake). The guide price might seem overpriced/an unnecessary expense for one of the easier walks, but it was well worth it for the 6 hour trek to and from Kabbale which absolutely would not have been possible without one. While I did not have to organise the guide myself, it seems like it would be best to do this in advance should you plan your own visit.If you go, I would suggest ensuring you organize transport to and from, as I really don't think Uber or PickMe would have cars avaliable there, based on what I saw (and contrary to what the apps might suggest showing the car icons as being nearby). My car was 20,000 return to Galle, which included the driver waiting for me at the entrance (so it was a good 8 hour shift for him). There is a bathing area right near the start of the trails. There is a small and ramshackle concrete hut for changing if you bring your suit (though there are also washrooms a short walk away). I am not sure about bathing at the waterfalls, I only went to Waterfall 1 and it didn't seem like it would have been an issue (though I did not try this). The Kabbale peak was good for an excercise trek, but if I were to have a do over, I think I would opt for one of the 'easier' treks, not because of ease but because I think I may have had more luck spotting birds and animals this way. The next longest trek would have been to Waterfall 2, which was 7 km round trip and as noted, the last bit of which is properly through forest trails (a la bushwacking style perhaps though I cannt be sure).
title: Good for exercise, hit and miss for fauna

body: I came by car having phoned ahead the previous day to ensure a guide would be available at 6.30 am. We managed to find 19 species of birds on the shorter of the two trips ( packages ) on offer in three hours. It cost 660 Rupees to enter and a further 1000 for the compulsory guide. I stayed on the main road and didn't go on the climb down to the caves or to the waterfall due to a dodgy knee. You don't encounter leeches this way, but I had a bag of salt ready just in case a few attached themselves to me. You don't need leech socks or boots as plastic sandals will do fine if you have salt with you. You will see incredible spider's webs and lots of beautiful butterflies as well as all the birds. My guide Rubica knew the names of lots of the trees and spotted two species of endemic lizards. We found the Spot-winged Thrush in the undergrowth and also saw Malabar Trogans, Flame Minivets, several species of Bulbuls and Flycatchers, Scimitar Babbler and Dark-fronted Babbler. The forest is only secondary growth recovering from deforestation some 30 - 40 years ago and is nowhere near as impressive as Sinharaja. It's still a great place for an early morning bird-watching expedition. Bring your own food and water as there is nothing there but the forest.

body: Kanneliya was an 80 minute drive from Unawatuna and we arrived at 7.30 to meet our pre-arranged guide. We opted for the 3 hour walk, which took in the waterfall and the giant tree. Our guide was great at spotting wildlife, which we would otherwise have missed - tiny lizards, chameleons, monkeys, snakes and a variety of exotic birds. Most of the path is straightforward but parts are steep and there are quite a lot of steps around the waterfall. You do need a reasonable level of fitness for this walk because the humidity of the rainforest saps energy and we were glad we didn't opt for the 5-6 hour trek! We were provided with leech socks and our guide checked our feet regularly so none found their way into our shoes but my husband did get bitten on his chest and it was promptly removed by the guide. I would definitely recommend an early arrival because there were busloads of locals arriving as we were leaving at 11am. Our hotel arranged the guide in advance (you cannot enter the forest without a guide) and a driver, at a total cost of 11,000Rps. We were also offered lunch at an extra 3000Rps but didn't bother because we left mid-morning. We were glad our hotel arranged everything because the entry to the rainforest, and other attractions in Sri Lanka for that matter, is not as organised as it could be and you could find yourself paying for something you don't want or not being able to get in at all if you arrive early or at a busy time and there are no guides available.
title: Great experience

body: I really wish I had done more research before attempting this hike. It is truly a spectacular reserve with so much to appreciate. However, due to the rain the night before, we were not prepared for the leeches. Our guide was prepared with a bar of soap, which he explained only once the leeches started attaching themselves, was used to deter the leeches. The little critters are extremely quick and make their way onto your shoes and into your socks in no time. Although not too much of a fuss for the adults, the leeches caused a bit of hysteria for the children. Especially that moment a leech pops in your shoe with blood soaking your socks. Leech drama aside it was still an awesome experience. Our guide was extremely knowledgeable on various flora and took the time to listen to all our questions. His English was limited but did his best to help us understand. We did see two purple leaf monkeys, loads of frogs, jungle fowl, large scary spiders and little lizards. We crawled through a bat cave and crossed streams with plenty fish and fresh water prawns. I loved seeing all the pitcher plants and the beautiful waterfalls. The leeches were mostly on the path towards the second waterfall. We were wearing shorts and the leeches quickly found their way onto our legs. Our hike took 5 hours and my children are 11 and 9 years old, they coped well with the walking even the most steep incline with little footpaths. Their biggest concern were the blood sucking alien-like critters on the floor. I know that we will be talking about this hike for a long time. Wear long trousers, leech socks and good walking shoes. Take an umbrella for rain and an acidic soap to rub on your legs and feet to deter leeches. In my opinion, Children younger than 8 should not attempt the walk to the second waterfall.
title: Hike

body: Kanneliya or KDN is a rain forest reserve in the Southern Province of Sri Lanka. Identified as one of the most floristically rich areas in South Asia. The forest is situated 35km northwest of the City of Galle; and is a major catchment area for two of the most important rivers in southern Sri Lanka, Gin Ganga and Nilwala Ganga. The Kanneliya Forest reserve has large number of endemic flora and fauna. The forest also harbours numerous medicinal plants and rare plants within the forest; including yellow vine (Concinium fenestratum), Salacia reticulata, heart-leaved moonseed (Tinospora cordifolia), coarse tassel fern (Lycopodium Squarrosum), and coarse tassel fern (Lycopodium phlegmaria)Visitors to Kanneliya should first visit the Forestry Department building housed within the jungle. The building also has a dormitory with bunk beds, where visitors can choose to stay overnight. They also provide traditional meals in the cafeteria made from fresh local produce. So spending a whole day looking at the attractions is a good idea too. The Kanneliya Rainforest Has more beautiful sights to see. There is an observation platform built halfway up the trunk so that visitors can see the wonders of Kanneliya from a height.

body: We did this as a trip from Galle through a company called Pepper Life. It was about an hour and a half drive away from Galle. We did the 8km trek with trekker and guides. It was an easy walk, not strenuous and throughout our time there we were continually pointed out flora and fauna within their natural habitats. We saw some amazing sights, and being British, we were in awe of the sights,sounds and smells of the rainforest so different to our home environment. Our guides were brilliant- very knowledgeable and passionate about the forest. They were very well prepared- leech socks if we needed them and home made cake for our mid morning snack!!! The experience we had opted for included a Sri Lankan home cooked lunch eaten in the river at the end of the trek. What can I say? Home cooked food, feet cooling down in the river, fish swimming around our toes, monkeys in the trees, birds, butterflies......who could ask for anything more. Go to Kanneliya, you won't be disappointed.

body: A relatively less visited and a younger rain-forest in Sri Lanka, Kanneliya would enable you to connect with wonders of nature. The location is easily accessible through the southern highway and is a max 2 hour drive from colombo if you use a private vehicle. At the park entrance, you have to pay a nominal fee for entry and should pay and obtain the services of a local guide (the price varies on the trek distance). There are a couple of paths to chose from, with different difficulty levels that would range from a casual uphill walk on a road / paths to more difficult treks through the forest paths itself. The time taken could vary from about 4 hours, to a full-day. You will be able to enjoy the flora and fauna, and it is a really calming and peaceful experience during the weekdays. But from what I understand, it can get pretty crowded and "not so calming" during weekends. There are many streams, and a few beautiful water-falls that rewards you after a tiring walk. (Bathing not allowed, but certainly wash your face and dip your toes :) )Once you are back, you can have your meals at the cafeteria (Bring your own food, as only snacks and drinks are available). You can also have a refreshing river bath in the stream closer to the park-entrance (within the park). Suggest that you take all your plastics, bottles and garbage to wherever you brought it from, and make sure that we keep the forest clean, and unpolluted..Aruna
title: Be with Nature

body: Kanneliya Forest Reserve is an excellent spot for easy hikes, picnics, and/or swim in the crystal clear water. The forest is about 2-3 hours drive from Colombo. Facilities are basic, but good. The trails are very easy to hike and well maintained. The forest was previously logged (last logging in 1988), but has recovered quickly and there are some very beautiful and large trees to enjoy. Lots of birds and monkeys. And some leeches in wet areas.... be prepared with repellent or leech pants. Finally, note that the forest gets very large numbers of visitors on weekends; try to visit on a week day for more peace and tranquility.

body: Kanneliya Rain Forest.Kannelya rain forest is just one of the Galle's many landmarks to discover. Tourists whom are seeking adventure based tourism locations in Sri Lanka tour in down south, the Kanneliya rain forest is ideal place for that. Probably it is more appropriate for a natural fresh water bath, Hiking, waterfalls and beautiful landscapes. It is a low land forest extends about 5306 ha. Galle is consisted of many major forest reservation complexes. Namely Sinharaja, Kanneliya, Dediyagala and Nakiyadeniya (KDN Complex), Kottawa, ect. Kanneliya Rain Forest located about 36 km to the northeast from Galle. And also it is tropical rain forest in Galle district. The mean annual rainfall is around 3750 mm. Kanneliya Rain Forest is well enriched with bio diversity. It may be second listed just because of the Sinharaja Forest. Kanneliya Rain Forest is one of the most attractive tourist site in Galle district, Sri Lanka. If you visit is place you can visit these places and share the experience. * Cave Trail – distance : 1.6 km, time 1 hour* Anagimala Ella Trail – distance : 2.5 km, time 3 hours* Elephant Creeper (Yodha Puswela) Trail – distance : 2.5 km, time 3 hours* Narangas Ella Trail – distance : 5.4 km, time 6 hours* Giant Nawada Tree Trail – distance : 3.8km, time 3 hours* Kabbale Mountain Trail – 5.5 km, time 6 hours – considered the most difficult trek from all.You want to take a entrance ticket and hire a Kanneliya Guidethen you can enter this natural forest. In additionally Kanneliya rain forest ideal for fresh water bath. You can see fresh water fish (Some fish are endemic to Sri Lanka).Kanneliya rain forest occupied the interfluves between two rivers, the Nilwala Ganga and Gin Ganga. If consist of a series of ridges and valleys and elevation ranges from 60 – 425m above mean sea level. The mean monthly temperature is around 27°c with a diurnal range of 4°c-5°c. Maximum temperature has been recorded from mid-March to mid-May. ‘Gin ganga’ river is the main water supplement to the Kanneliya forest. Multitudes of endemic plants are preserved in the forest. As the forest is comprised with many attractions, you don’t have to investigate whole the area as they can be reached easily. The Anagimale fall is just 2km from the entrance. By the way several forest conservation projects are carrying out to preserve this natural diversity. Hence ward the forest department is also supporting them. Due to a reforestation program carried out in early 1970’s has recovered a little. It is evident that once you harmed to the environment it takes more time to be recovered.December to February is the most suitable months to travel as it gets the highest rain fall. Usually the streams are running with their full force of water through the jungle and create beautiful cascades and sceneries. It will make you sense. You can bath in cool natural streams. Eventually it will energize you. Somehow you will have to take care of leechs. Bring some lime with you and if you are beaten, put few drops on the leech and it will leave you at once. Some of the popular pools located at the forest are the natural pool behind the Kanneliya forest resort, the pool in front of the Kanneliya conservation centre (KCC) and the pool behind the KCC. Tourists looking for hiking are encouraged to visit the forest during the months of March or April as it may get reduced the rain fall. There are two traces used for hiking. You can select either route to Kabbale Mountain or the route through ‘Narangas’ ella. The gigantic ‘Navada’ tree is on the same way. A panoramic view of the entire area can be entertained at the top of the Kabbale hill. The light filtered through the forest canopy and tree leaves is unmemorable.Public access to Kanneliya is allowed through the forest department managed conservation center located close to Galle-Udugama-Neliwa road at Koralegama, PanangalaRoute1: Colombo -> Kalutara (Katukurunda) [45km on A2] -> Nagoda [3km on B008] -> Mathugama [5km on B308 & 11km on B8] -> Horawala [5km on B3] -> Moragala [7km] -> Palewatta [8km on B3] -> Pitigala [10km on B3] -> Udugama [24km via Mapalagama] -> Panangala [6km on B156] ->Koralegama -> Kanneliya Conservation Centre [2km](approximately 125km)Route2: Colombo -> Galle [120km on A2] ->Udugama [40km] ->Panangala [6km on B156] ->Koralegama -> Kanneliya Conservation Centre [2km](approximately 165km)Entrance Tickets Before enter the Kanneliya rain forest the tourists have to pay for entrance ticket from forest department side office. Entrance ticket value and add 11% VAT (Value Added Tax) for total ticket value. Foreign tourist ticket values are given below. Entrance TicketsCategory Ticket value (Rs.) VAT Total Ticket value (Rs)Foreign Adult 575/= + 11% 638.25Foreign Child 290/= + 11% 321.90 Source: Kanneliya Side Ofiice – Forest Department Kanneliya rain forest guides charges With the entrance tickets the tourists have to pay Kanneliya guides fee also. As a community base tourism government introduce and established Kanneliya guide association. After this association village peoples’ can give their contribution to protect the Kanneliya rain forest in additionaly the village peoples’ can earn additionally income to their life. body: Had a great time - some of walking a bit strenuous in the heat but well worth it when you get to waterfalls. body: The highest biodiversity found in sri Lanka, kanneliya is a place accessible within hours from Colombo Sri Lanka.The hike through the thick rain forest is quite exciting and refreshing. there is an old road which was built years back when the forest reserve was under the Ceylon Plywood corporation. However, vehicles are not allowed inside the reserve. hiking could be through the foot paths within the jungle as well as through small streams and ricers within the jungle.The bio diversity is quite evident with plenty of flora ans fauna to be seen without much effort. For bird lovers kanneliya is ideal with many native and low wet land birds around to be seen.Leaches and the rough terrain are the main draw backs and if you are up for the challenge, the hike is one of a kind.Plenty of streams and small water ways and water falls full of fish and other aquatic animals in the jungle. however, bathing is allowed only just at the entrance due to pollution of water.Tip; a special kind of soap is available around the shops in the area which is ideal for leaches.

body: Visited there in April with a group of 15 people. Kanneliya is the largest of KDN the low land rain forest complex( Kanneliya - Nakiyadeniya -Dadiyagala). It is one of the most biologically diverse areas in Sri Lanka. Present Kanneliya is a product of selective logging that had happened in 1970s. Gin river is the main feeder to the region.There will be few standard nature trails out of which, "kabbale mountain and Anagimale falls" circular trail is the longest. It is about 6.5km. So if you are planning for that better to start early. You are allowed to take take your lunch with you.You can have it near anagimale falls.There are two restautants near by and they will arrange meals for your orders. We have to pay 1000 for the guide.We were are lucky get a good tracker, he explained a lot about the forest and diffent animal and plant species. At the end of the trail we had a natural bath near the forest Conservation Centre. So if you are planning to visit kanneliya, go there early, get a good tracker, equipt with leech protection😆 and then you can enjoy the trail...

body: Kanneliya can be reached within 3 hours of journey from Colombo via southern expressway (take Kurundugaha hatapma exit). It is a Sri Lankan low country evergreen forest with thick vegetation and number of streams running through the forest. According to the information I collected the forest once was connected to the Sinharaja so shares a similar bio diversity.Trail lies within the forest leads to a series of beautiful waterfalls and the terrain is not too difficult. recommended for kids and beginners. Total altitude gain is about 50m (according to what I felt... no apparatus used. Please bear with me if I am wrong :-))Forest is filled with number of interesting flora and my greatest attraction was fresh water fish found in the streams. Exotic fish inherited to SL was available including fish such as Puntius pleurotaenia.Word of advise, watch out for the leaches :-)

Rain Forest worth a visit
body: This rain forest reserve is about an hour outside Galle. It is much like national parks in the U.S., which is to say, pretty basic. But it does show a rain forest habitat, and our guide was pretty good at spotting assorted creatures and flora that were unique and unusual. Entry costs 440 rupees (about $3.50), and there are several options for guided tours -- a two hour walk to the first water fall, about 2.5km each way, or a three hour walk to the second fall, about 7km, each way. It was a typically hot and humid day. We had driven to the park from Ambalangoda, where we were staying at the Max Wadiya (see separate review), which was about 1.5-2 hours away. So we opted for the two hour guided walk -- calling it a hike would be presumptuous, though it was on a gentle incline all the way. The cost of the guide was an additional 880 rupees ($7 for both of us). The guide was capable and pointed out little critters and flora that would have certainly escaped our eyes.The finale, so to speak, was the waterfall itself. The path to the water falls from the main path was the only part that made us regret wearing sandals instead of sneakers. Even so, it was no big deal. The falls are not that big, but very refreshing. After a 5-10 minutes dipping our feet, it was back up the rough path to the main, well-maintained path and downhill to the entrance, about a 15-20 minute easy walk. We saw monkeys, salamanders, lizards of different descriptions unusual plant life and trees. May not be for everyone, but it is a great example of south Asian rain forests. Appropriate for families with kids as well as couple.
